# Anthony Albanese Quotes

May 12, 2025 by [Magnus Holloway](https://quotesoftheday.org/author/magnus-holloway/ "View all posts by Magnus Holloway")

Anthony Albanese has made a significant mark in Australian politics. His words inspire many, highlighting his vision and commitment to the nation. Here are some memorable quotes from him that reflect his beliefs, values, and aspirations for Australia.

### Leadership and Vision

Albanese often speaks about leadership and the future of Australia. His quotes remind us of the importance of unity and progress.

🔹 “A strong economy is built on a foundation of fairness and opportunity for all.”  
🔹 “We must work together to create a brighter future for every Australian.”  
🔹 “Leadership is not just about making decisions. It’s about making a difference.”
🔹 “True progress is measured by the well-being of our communities.”  
🔹 “Hope is not a strategy, but it is the fuel that drives our ambitions.”

### Commitment to Equality

Albanese is a staunch advocate for equality and social justice. His words resonate with the need for inclusivity.

🔹 “Equality is not just a principle; it’s a necessity for a fair society.”  
🔹 “Every voice matters, and every person deserves respect.”  
🔹 “We rise or fall together. Let’s lift each other up.”  
🔹 “Diversity is our strength, not our weakness.”  
🔹 “A fair society is one where everyone has the chance to succeed.”

### Environmental Responsibility

Albanese understands the urgency of addressing climate change. His quotes reflect a commitment to protecting the environment.

🔹 “We owe it to future generations to protect our planet.”  
🔹 “Climate action is not just an option; it’s an obligation.”  
🔹 “Sustainable development is the key to our future.”
🔹 “Investing in renewable energy is investing in our children’s future.”  
🔹 “Nature doesn’t wait. We must act now.”

### Economic Growth

Economic growth is at the forefront of Albanese’s agenda. His quotes highlight the importance of innovation and resilience.

🔹 “A thriving economy creates opportunities for everyone.”  
🔹 “Innovation is the heartbeat of a successful nation.”  
🔹 “Resilience is not just about bouncing back; it’s about moving forward.”  
🔹 “We must adapt to change to stay competitive.”  
🔹 “Investing in education is investing in our economy.”

### Community and Connection

Albanese emphasizes the importance of community. His words reflect a deep connection to the people of Australia.

🔹 “Community is where our strength lies.”  
🔹 “We must listen to the concerns of our citizens.”  
🔹 “Together, we can build a more connected society.”  
🔹 “A strong community is the backbone of a strong nation.”
🔹 “Let’s celebrate our differences and come together as one.”

### Final Thoughts

Anthony Albanese’s quotes offer a glimpse into his vision for Australia. They remind us of the power of unity, equality, and progress. His words encourage us to think about our role in shaping the future. How can we contribute to a fairer, more sustainable society?

In a world filled with challenges, Albanese’s quotes inspire hope and action. They serve as a call to each of us to be part of the change we wish to see. Let’s take these words to heart and work towards a better tomorrow.

# Prime Minister Anthony Albanese says sexuality and gender census questions ‘weren’t appropriate’

* Sep 02 2024
* Written by [PinkNews Reporter](https://www.thepinknews.com/author/pinknews-reporter/)

* Share
  
  [](https://twitter.com/share?text=https://www.thepinknews.com/2024/09/02/2026-australian-census-lgbtq-questions/) [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.thepinknews.com/2024/09/02/2026-australian-census-lgbtq-questions/) [](https://reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2024%2F09%2F02%2F2026-australian-census-lgbtq-questions%2F)  [](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2024%2F09%2F02%2F2026-australian-census-lgbtq-questions%2F) [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?
mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thepinknews.com%2F2024%2F09%2F02%2F2026-australian-census-lgbtq-questions%2F)* Save for later
* Comment

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has spoken about the 2026 Australian census. (Getty)

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has said that the 2026 Australian census questions on sexuality and gender “weren’t appropriate”.

The prime minister said that the federal government informed the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) to cancel new census questions on sexuality, gender and diverse sex characteristics because they “weren’t appropriate.”

Last week, the [federal government announced](https://www.thepinknews.com/2024/08/27/australian-census-lgbt/) that Australia’s 2026 Census wouldn’t ask people about gender, sexual orientation, or diverse sex characteristics. Instead, the upcoming questions would fail to highlight topics important to the LGBTQ+ community, which [the 2021 Census](https://www.thepinknews.
com/2022/06/28/australia-census-same-sex-weddings/) was also criticised for.

The move incited outrage from the LGBTQ+ community and allies over the government’s initial decision to avoid “divisive debates”, and the prime minister [eventually made a U-turn](https://www.thepinknews.com/2024/08/30/australias-census-to-ask-about-sexuality-for-first-time-after-backlash/) on the choice.

However, the upcoming census will only include one question which is inclusive of the LGBTQ+ community, on sexuality.

On 1 September, the [prime minister](https://www.thepinknews.com/2024/03/19/anthony-albanese-school-laws/) refused to commit to reinstating all the draft questions but added that the government would work through issues with the ABS and the LGBTQ+ community.

He [said](https://www.abc.net.
au/news/2024-09-01/anthony-albanese-census-gender-identity-intersex/104296702) the previous census already included an “identity-type question”, but that “there should be something included about sexual orientation as well”.

Albanese said: “Quite clearly, what there should be is common-sense questions asked that are quite easily understood.

“The ABS was going to go out and test some questions on Monday…That’s why we put a pause on that so that we could consider appropriate questions that were easily understood by people when they get the census,” he continued.

“My government values every Australian, regardless of who they are, regardless of their sexuality, their race, their faith, their gender: we value every single Australian.”

Social Services Minister Amanda Rishworth said to [Sky News](https://ministers.dss.gov.
au/transcripts/15886) that the government was presented with questions “that were very complex in the census”, and suggested that the nation may not have been able to “understand and answer” the draft questions.

## ‘The census won’t include all Australians’

Equality Australia chief executive Anna Brown welcomed the inclusion of the question, but added that “the national snapshot of our nation must include all of us, not just some of us”.

Brown went on to say: “We’re happy the government has decided to include a sexual orientation question in the census, but until questions on gender identity and intersex people are included, the census won’t include all Australians.”

# Government Backflips On Decision To Omit LGBTQI+ Focused Questions In 2026 Census After Backlash

the Australian Bureau of Statistics Anthony Albanese Josh Burns Labor ABS

The government has backflipped on its decision to [not include LGBTIQ+-focused questions](https://www.pedestrian.tv/news/lgbtiq-census-questions-removed-2026/) in the upcoming 2026 census by declaring that it will include a whopping one question about sexuality.

After a [considerable amount of backlash](https://www.pedestrian.tv/news/australian-census-lgbtqi-2021/) from the [LGBTIQ+](https://www.pedestrian.
tv/news/tokyo-2020-more-lgbtq-athletes/) community, advocacy groups and Labor MP **Josh Burns** , Prime Minister **Anthony Albanese** confirmed to ABC radio on Friday morning that the census would include one question about sexual preference.

“We’ve been talking with the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and they’re going to test for a new question, one question about sexuality, sexual preference,” he said, per the [ABC](https://www.smh.com.au/national/australia-news-live-high-fire-danger-for-sydney-labor-mps-to-defy-albanese-on-sexuality-in-census-20240830-p5k6j4.html) .

When questioned on why the government decided to reverse their decision, Albanese said that the Labor government was more focused on including questions about the cost of living crisis and noted that the exact questions hadn’t been confirmed.

“We haven’t sat down and gone through, line by line, what questions will be asked in the census in two years time,” he said.
Burns, who called on the Prime Minister to reconsider his stance on including these questions, was happy with the government’s announcement.

“I definitely welcome the prime minister’s comments this morning. I think that they go to making sure people are counted, and I think that they go to the work that we’re doing to ensure that we are collecting the best data possible to feed into government services as part of the census,” he told ABC radio Melbourne, per the [ABC](https://www.smh.com.au/national/australia-news-live-high-fire-danger-for-sydney-labor-mps-to-defy-albanese-on-sexuality-in-census-20240830-p5k6j4.html) .

_Prime Minister Albanese at the Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras Parade in 2022. (Photo by Brendon Thorne/Getty Images)_

In case you missed it, the Albanese government came under fire earlier this week for the omission of questions about gender identity and sexuality in the 2026 census.
Rather than making an announcement, the government opted to confirm via the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) that the census would be the exact same as the census we took in 2021.

> Why has the federal gov stopped the ABS from including questions around gender, sexual orientation and intersex variation in the 2026 census? I mean, if the expression ‘you measure what you value’ holds true, that isn’t a good sign, hey.
> 
> — Wil Stracke (@WilStracke) [August 26, 2024](https://twitter.com/WilStracke/status/1827974496252510424?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

This decision went against promises Labor made during the last election to acknowledge and include sexuality, gender identity and intersex status within the next census. As a result, the LGBTQ+ community and advocacy groups spoke out, as they felt that without these questions the census was unable to accurately represent all Australians.
After the decision was made public, Macnamara MP Josh Burns spoke out against his own party to have the voices of his LGBTQ+ constituents heard.

“Macanamara is home to many LGBTIQA+ community members and I love being their MP and as part of that, I feel a responsibility to stand up for them,” he [said](https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/article/2024/aug/29/not-to-much-to-ask-for-people-to-be-counted-josh-burns-breaks-ranks-on-gender-and-sexuality-census-questions) .

“I’ve made it clear that the way we govern needs to be inclusive and the census is an important tool to gather data and feed that into government systems and services. For that to work the best it can, we need as few blind spots as possible, which is why I am asking the government to reconsider this decision.

“It is not too much to ask for people to be counted.”
